# `unitext` — specification

## Maturity

**Grade:** 3 · S3 E2 A2 H1 P3 · limited by scope (core), performance (not measured) *(generated by `zig build gen-catalog`)*

**Scope:** core — CPython `str` + `unicodedata`, Rust std (`str::to_lowercase`, `to_uppercase`) + `unicode-normalization`, Go `golang.org/x/text` (`unicode/norm`, `cases`, `runes`), ICU (surveyed 2026-11-09 from their documentation, not by reading their source; CPython and Rust were then RUN over the module's inputs, see Anchoring). What a pandas / polars string column user needs is here; what a Go or ICU user also expects and is missing (language-tailored case, word-boundary titlecase, `unicodedata.name`, segmentation) is under *What is deliberately not done* with reasons.

**Audit:** review 2026-11-09 · mutation 2026-11-20 (169/193, 24 eq) · src dbe811339f00fd41

**Hardening:** fuzz 2026-11-09 (300,000 runs clean in ReleaseSafe after the UR-1 fix, `UNITEXT_FUZZ`, 15 s; the harness is described under Anchoring; no planted-mutant check yet, see Open) · ct n/a — no secret: the module transforms caller-supplied text · panic 2026-11-09 (independent sweep of every pub entry point, `src/unit_test.zig` "sweep: …": per-code-point functions clamp any `u21` (surrogates, above U+10FFFF) to the default record before indexing; every string form decodes through `utf8.step`, whose reads are guarded by `i + k >= s.len`; the 256-byte emitter block is checked before each append; `ListOut` checks `bytes.len > cap - len` with `len <= cap` by construction; the normalization working buffer is capped by `max_segment` and the output by `max_output`, zero caps give `error.TooLarge` or an empty result; sort and compose are linear or n log n, Final_Sigma look-ahead crosses each case-ignorable run at most once; no finding, no `unreachable`/`assert` on a caller value)

**Performance:** not measured

**Known defects:** none recorded

**Downstream consumer:** no

**Where we are ahead:** a Zig implementation of all of it with no dependency; one explicit policy for ill-formed bytes shared by every function (CPython and Rust take a `str` and cannot receive them); allocation caps on every allocating form (CPython and Rust have none); `unaccent` with `ł ø đ ħ ŧ ı` and the ligatures in one call (Go and ICU need the transform chain, CPython has nothing) · **Where we are behind:** no language-tailored case (Turkish dotted I, Lithuanian), no word-boundary titlecase (polars `to_titlecase`, Go `cases.Title`), no streaming normalizer object (`Reader`/`Writer`; the writer forms stream the output but read the whole input slice), no `unicodedata.name`/`numeric`/`decomposition` (→ Backlog).

## What this module is, and what it is not

Unicode algorithms that operate on one UTF-8 string and need the Unicode Character Database: case mapping, normalization, accent folding and the `str.is*` classification. The tables are Unicode 18.0.0 (`unicode_version`), generated, with no runtime file access and no allocation in a lookup. It exists because pandas (Python `str`) and polars (Rust `str`) do Unicode case mapping by default, so a Zig dataframe that does only ASCII gives different answers on real text, and because nothing in zig-libs had case *mapping* or *normalization* (`regex` holds simple case-fold orbits for `(?i)`, `validate` the sets of code points that change under lower/upper; neither can map).

Not here: collation (UCA, sort keys), grapheme / word / sentence segmentation, the bidi algorithm, IDNA / UTS #46, East Asian display width, confusables, Unicode names, language-tailored case rules — see "What is deliberately not done". The single-property lookups of `unicodedata` (`decimal`, `digit`, `numeric`, `bidirectional`, `mirrored`, `east_asian_width`, `decomposition`) are here.

## Wire format / algorithm

**Decoding.** UTF-8 is read with Unicode 18 Table 3-7; an ill-formed stretch is split into maximal subparts (§3.9). `Options.invalid_utf8`: `.reject` returns `error.InvalidUtf8` (output already written stays in the writer); `.replace` writes U+FFFD per maximal subpart; `.pass_through` copies the bad bytes and treats them as an uncased, non-ignorable, combining-class-0 unit that ends any normalization segment.

**Case mapping** (`case.zig`). Per code point: the simple mapping of UnicodeData (fields 12-14; titlecase falls back to uppercase) overridden by the unconditional entries of SpecialCasing.txt that differ from it (ß → SS / Ss, ŉ → ʼN, İ → i + U+0307, ǰ, ΐ, ΰ, the FB00-FB17 ligatures, the Greek iota-subscript forms; 103 uppercase, 49 titlecase, 1 lowercase entry; 18.0 added U+1DF95 LIGATURE LONG S WITH DESCENDER S → SS / Ss); folding is CaseFolding.txt C + S (simple) and C + F (full). Context: **Final_Sigma** (§3.13) for `lower`, `title`, `capitalize`, `swapcase` (and Σ reached by them): Σ becomes ς when the previous non-Case_Ignorable code point is Cased and the next non-Case_Ignorable one is not; the previous side is tracked while scanning, the next side by a look-ahead that skips Case_Ignorable code points (linear overall: a run of ignorables is crossed by at most one Σ before it). No other conditional entry is applied (Turkic `tr`/`az`, Lithuanian `lt`).

- `title`: CPython's rule: the first Cased code point after a non-Cased one is titlecased (full), every other lowercased, "Cased" being the Cased property; so `they're` → `They'Re` and `ǆungla` → `ǅungla`.
- `capitalize`: first code point titlecased (full: `ß` → `Ss`, `ǆ` → `ǅ`), the rest lowercased (3.8+ CPython).
- `swapcase`: Uppercase-property code points lowercased (full, with Final_Sigma), Lowercase-property ones uppercased (full), everything else unchanged (so `ǅ` stays).
- `casefold`: full folding; for caseless matching, not display.

**Normalization** (`norm.zig`, UAX #15). Decompose each code point (Hangul syllables arithmetically, the rest from the table of full recursive canonical / compatibility decompositions), cut the text into segments at every starter whose NFC_QC is Yes, stably sort each run of non-starters by Canonical_Combining_Class (insertion sort up to 16 marks, `std.sort.block` beyond), and for NFC / NFKC compose in place with the UAX #15 algorithm (blocked-by-intervening-class rule; Hangul L+V, LV+T algorithmically; the 961 primary composites, the Full_Composition_Exclusion ones left out by the generator). `quickCheck` is the NFC_QC / NFKC_QC / NFD_QC / NFKD_QC walk with the canonical-order check; `isNormalized` answers from it when it can and otherwise normalizes segment by segment and compares with the input without building the output. ASCII runs are copied without a lookup (the last ASCII byte before a non-ASCII one is kept in the segment, since `e` + U+0301 composes; a comptime check proves no composition pair ends in ASCII).

**`unaccent`.** NFD; drop code points of General_Category Mn; map the letters of `unaccent_letters` to ASCII; with `expand_ligatures` (default **on**: PostgreSQL's `unaccent` and ICU's Latin-ASCII do it, sklearn's `strip_accents` does not) expand `unaccent_expansions`; NFC. The two lists are derived by the generator from the UCD *names*, never copied from another project's rules file. A name `LATIN SMALL|CAPITAL LETTER|LIGATURE <base> [WITH <modifiers>]`, or a small capital `LATIN LETTER SMALL CAPITAL <base> …` / `LATIN SMALL CAPITAL LETTER <base> …` (which folds to the capital letter, as Latin-ASCII does), of a code point with no canonical decomposition is read as its base: the modifiers (hook, stroke, bar, tail, flourish …) are dropped as NFD + dropping marks drops an accent, unless they name a second `LETTER` (UR-1). `unaccent_letters` (329 entries; 304 in 17.0.0) = a base that is one letter A-Z (ð ø đ ħ ł ŧ ŀ ɓ ƒ …, ᴀ ɢ ʀ …) or one of the named one-letter bases `NAMED_LETTERS`: DOTLESS I, DOTLESS J, ETH, LONG S (ſ → s), the letters of their own alphabet's order whose ASCII stand-in is fixed by orthography or transliteration practice — ENG (ŋ → n), KRA (ĸ → q, the Greenlandic 1973 reform), OPEN E, IOTA, U BAR, AFRICAN D, SCRIPT G — and the glyph variants BROKEN L, INSULAR D / F / T, MIDDLE-WELSH V, BARRED B. `unaccent_expansions` (69 code points, 67 in 17.0.0, under `expand_ligatures`) = the named several-letter bases `NAMED_EXPANSIONS`: AE, OE, IJ, SHARP S, THORN, TH, FF, FI, FL, FFI, FFL, ST, LONG S T, the medievalist and Americanist ligature letters AA AO AU AV AY OO VY UE HV OI MIDDLE-WELSH LL, the IPA digraphs DB QP DZ TS LS LZ (`… DIGRAPH`), plus the twelve digraphs Ǆ ǅ ǆ Ǉ ǈ ǉ Ǌ ǋ ǌ Ǳ ǲ ǳ by exact name (`NAMED_DIGRAPHS`); capitals expand to capitals, titlecase to titlecase: Æ → AE, ǅ → Dz, Ꜳ → AA, ɶ → OE. Every list is checked against ICU's Latin-ASCII (Anchoring). Marks of **every** script that are Mn are removed (Hebrew points, Arabic harakat, Devanagari signs of category Mn), not only Latin accents; compatibility mappings are not applied.

**Classification.** CPython's definitions, from the tables: `isAlpha` = category Lm Lt Lu Ll Lo; `isAlphabetic` / `isAlphabeticCp` = the Alphabetic derived property of `DerivedCoreProperties.txt` (L + Nl + Other_Alphabetic, so many combining vowel signs of category Mc / Mn count; Rust `char::is_alphabetic`, polars `cs.alpha()`; NOT Python's `isalpha`; checked for every code point against the file's ranges, `src/testdata/alphabetic_ranges.txt`); `isDecimal` = Numeric_Type Decimal; `isDigit` = Decimal or Digit; `isNumeric` = any Numeric_Type (this includes the CJK numerals such as 三, because `DerivedNumericType.txt` includes the Unihan values, as CPython does); `isAlnum` = any of the four; `isSpace` = Bidi_Class WS, B, S or category Zs; `isPrintable` = not Cc Cf Cs Co Cn Zl Zp and of Zs only the ASCII space; `isUpper` / `isLower` / `isTitle` as CPython's loops over the Uppercase / Lowercase properties and Lt. Empty string: false for all but `isPrintable` and `isAscii`. An ill-formed stretch counts as U+FFFD under `.replace` and `.pass_through`.

**Single-property lookups** (`props.zig`; CPython `unicodedata`). `decimalValue` / `digitValue` (`?u8`) and `numericValue` (`?Numeric`, an exact `num / den`, `toF64()` is CPython's float; the Numeric_Value comes from `DerivedNumericValues.txt`, so the CJK numerals have one, and U+0F33 is -1/2); `bidiClass` (`?BidiClass`, UnicodeData's field, null where UnicodeData lists no entry: CPython's `''`, the unassigned defaults of DerivedBidiClass.txt are not applied); `isMirrored`; `eastAsianWidth` (the value of EastAsianWidth.txt, `.n` for everything it does not list, as CPython); `decomposition` (the one-level mapping of UnicodeData field 5 with its `<tag>` as data, null for none; `normalize` uses the full recursive tables) and `decompositionText` (CPython's string form, a Hangul syllable spelled as its jamo as CPython does). A value above U+10FFFF reads as the default record (null / `.n` / false).

**Tables** (`tables.zig`, `tools/ucd_gen/gen.py`). Every per-code-point table is three-stage (`vals[leaf[(t2[(t1[cp>>(a+b)]<<b)|((cp>>a)&mb)]<<a)|(cp&ma)]]`, shifts chosen per table by size): `gcflags` 23.2 KB (category, Uppercase / Lowercase / Cased / Case_Ignorable / space / Alphabetic, Numeric_Type; the Alphabetic bit cost 132 B), `norm` 12.0 KB (ccc, quick-check values), `decomp` 50.7 KB + 25.7 KB pool + `compose_pairs` 11.5 KB, `lower` / `upper` / `title` / `fold` 3.7-4.1 KB each + the `special_*` lists (about 5 KB), `unaccent_*` about 3 KB, `uprops` (Bidi_Class, Bidi_Mirrored, East_Asian_Width) 20 KB, `numrec` 9 KB, `rawdecomp` 59 KB + 24 KB pool. A `look` above U+10FFFF reads U+10FFFF (a noncharacter), so a `u21` argument cannot index out of range.

## Limits and refusals

- `Options.max_output` (default 1 GiB) caps an allocating result in bytes: `error.TooLarge` (the cap is checked before each append, so a hostile input cannot make the module allocate more than the cap plus one block). Case mapping grows UTF-8 text by at most 3x, NFKD of U+FDFA by 11x. Pinned by `unit_test.zig` "caps …" and the fuzz harness (a cap of exactly the result length succeeds, one byte less is `TooLarge`).
- `Options.max_segment` (default 16,777,216 code points = 64 MiB of working buffer) caps one normalization segment: a starter followed by that many marks is `error.TooLarge`; real text has segments of a few code points. CPython and Rust have no such cap. Stream-Safe Text Format is not enforced.
- Writer forms stream and ignore `max_output`; a failing writer is `error.WriteFailed` at any size (fuzzed with every capacity of the lowercase output).
- No consumer-reachable panic: every pub function is total on any bytes and any `u21`; the only assertions are comptime (GeneralCategory count equals the table's, no composition pair ends in ASCII, unaccent expansions never longer than their source, which the in-place filter relies on).
- `isNormalized` under `.replace` and `.pass_through` counts an ill-formed stretch as neutral (a starter that is its own normal form), so `isNormalized("\xFF", .nfc, .{ .invalid_utf8 = .replace })` is true although `normalize` would write U+FFFD.
- `max_segment = 0` fails a text that reaches a normalization segment (`"aé"`) but not ASCII-only text, which is copied without entering one.
- Thread safety: no global state; every function is reentrant.

## Performance

Not measured (no bench). Size, ReleaseSmall, stripped, single-threaded, `std.heap.page_allocator`, a program that reads one argument and prints the result: baseline (copy the argument) 120,632 B; calling only `lower` 149,912 B (+29,280 B); calling only `normalize` (NFKC) 226,560 B (+105,928 B). Unused tables are not linked (Zig compiles only what is referenced).

Case mappings: 41 code points (those 4, the 4 new capitals, U+1DF95 and 32 new Latin Extended-G letters in 16 case pairs); case folding: 21 (the capitals of those pairs, and U+1DF95 → U+00DF simple / `ss` full). Anchors for them: NormalizationTest.txt 18.0.0 for normalization; nothing foreign for case and classification (CPython is 16.0, Rust 17.0) — they are pinned only by the generator reading the UCD files (`gen.py -check`) and the per-code-point property test against `alphabetic_ranges.txt`. `unaccent`: 18.0 adds 25 letters and 2 expansions by the same name rules (Latin Extended-G and a Latin Extended-D capital, e.g. U+1DF72 O WITH CURL → O, U+1DF2E DZ DIGRAPH WITH PALATAL HOOK → dz); Latin-ASCII (Unicode 17) does not know them, the oracle reports them as `not-in-oracle` (163 code points new in the Latin blocks, the rest of the classes unchanged). Everything in `vectors_test.zig` is replayed in the ordinary test lane. Not anchored by a foreign oracle (pinned by examples and properties only): `unaccent` on strings (its lists are anchored per code point above, the steps NFD / NFC by Unicode's test), `title` word runs beyond CPython's rule (anchored: CPython's), the invalid-UTF-8 policies (Unicode §3.9 and the same boundaries as `std.unicode`, tested exhaustively on short strings in `utf8.zig`), the caps, the writer forms. The fuzz harness (see *Verification*) has no independent value oracle; values come from the vectors.

**Anchor grade:** class A · oracle EXTERNAL

## Verification

- **Run:** `scripts/modtest unitext`; the vector replays are part of the ordinary lane. `zig build run-example-unitext`
  runs the consumer example.
- **Unicode's own test:** `NormalizationTest.txt` (Parts 0-5, the five invariants per line, plus "every code point not
  in Part 1 is invariant") and the Hangul L V T arithmetic (`src/vectors_test.zig`).
- **Foreign oracles:** the CPython and Rust vector files, replayed by `src/vectors_test.zig` (every code point of the
  tables' intersection, and seeded strings); producers and what each covers are listed under *Anchoring*. By hand:
  `tools/latin_ascii_diff.py` (ICU `uconv -x Latin-ASCII`, fails on an unadopted letter or a stale `ARBITRARY`
  entry) and `gen.py -check` (the generated tables against the UCD files, fetched by `tools/ucd_gen/fetch.sh` into a
  gitignored directory).
- **Unit tests** (`src/unit_test.zig`, `src/props.zig`, `src/ucd.zig`): full case mappings, Final_Sigma, İ, ß / ŉ / ǰ /
  ligatures / Greek iota subscript; `title` / `capitalize` / `swapcase` / `casefold` Python semantics; per-code-point
  simple mappings; the standard normalization examples; `isNormalized` and `quickCheck`; each invalid-UTF-8 policy;
  the caps (errors, never a panic); writer forms streaming the same bytes and reporting writer failure; inputs
  crossing the 256-byte emit block and the 64-byte direct-write threshold; classification against CPython's
  documented behaviour; every `unaccent` rule class (titlecase digraphs, the twelve DZ / LJ / NJ digraphs, letters
  without `WITH` in their name, named bases under modifiers, small capitals, medieval glyph variants, ligature
  letters and IPA digraphs, the letters left alone); `isAlphabeticCp` for every code point against the ranges of
  `DerivedCoreProperties.txt` (`src/testdata/alphabetic_ranges.txt`).
- **Decoding** (`src/utf8.zig`): maximal subparts and every Table 3-7 boundary; `step` agrees with `std.unicode` on
  every scalar value and its validity with `utf8ValidateSlice` on all short strings.
- **Panic sweep** (`unit_test.zig`, "sweep: …"): every per-code-point function is total on hostile `u21` values;
  zero caps and empty inputs give errors or empty results, never a trap.
- **Fuzz:** deterministic driver, `UNITEXT_FUZZ=<runs>[,<first seed>]` (`src/fuzz_test.zig`). An input is a short
  UTF-8-ish string drawn from classes that hit every branch: ASCII, accented letters, Greek sigma contexts, combining
  marks of every class, Hangul jamo and syllables, ß / ŉ / ligatures / U+FDFA (expanding), case-ignorables and
  ill-formed bytes. The properties are the algebra of the four forms (NFC∘NFD = NFC …, idempotence, `isNormalized` ⇔
  unchanged), the three policies (`.reject` fails exactly on ill-formed input, `.replace` output is well-formed,
  `.pass_through` never fails and keeps the bad bytes), the caps at the exact boundary (a cap of the result length
  succeeds, one byte less is `TooLarge`), writer failure at every capacity, idempotent `casefold` and an NFC,
  ASCII-only `unaccent` result on Latin input. A fixed seed run with reach checks is in every test run. It has no
  independent value oracle; the values come from the vectors.
- **Constant time:** n/a — no secret: the module transforms caller-supplied text.
- **Mutation:** one whole-module run over every file but the generated `tables.zig` (193 mutants: one per condition and
  operator class in `utf8`, `common`, `norm`, `case`, `props`, `ucd`, `unaccent`), 169 killed, 24 equivalent (lead-byte masks,
  stable-sort choice, redundant quick-check shortcuts, guards behind the segment cut, the Cased = Upper | Lower | Lt identity;
  the tests that pin those facts are in `unit_test.zig`), none open. It found real gaps, now tests: the emit block's flush
  points and the order of direct writes, the Hangul range edges, `max_segment` with ASCII-only input, ill-formed bytes
  inside `isNormalized`, `title` / `capitalize` after an ill-formed stretch, `isPrintableCp` for surrogates, `isAscii` at
  0x80.
- **Audit:** the card's `**Audit:**` line is the current score, cumulative over that whole-module run and the delta runs
  after it.

## What is deliberately not done

- **Language-tailored case mapping** (Turkish / Azeri dotted and dotless I, Lithuanian dot retention; SpecialCasing's conditional entries; Go `cases.Lower(language.Turkish)`, ICU locale `CaseMap`). *Not now.* CPython, Rust and polars/pandas do not apply them either (their `lower` is locale-independent), so a pandas / polars user sees none; adding a `locale` option later is a table of 9 conditional entries and three contexts (After_I, Before_Dot, More_Above). No consumer has asked.
- **Word-boundary titlecase** (polars `str.to_titlecase`, Go `cases.Title`, ICU titlecase with a word `BreakIterator`). *Not now.* It needs UAX #29 word-break tables, which exist only inside `regex`; polars' exact boundary rule could not be verified here (polars is not installed), so no vectors could be produced. `title` is CPython's. See Backlog.
- **`unicodedata.name` / `lookup`.** *Never* in this module: the name table is over 1 MB of text, against a module whose point is a small table set; a consumer that needs names reads the UCD.
- **Collation (UCA), IDNA / UTS #46, confusables, the bidi algorithm, East Asian display width (`wcwidth`).** *Not now / never* by module: none is a method of Python `str`, Rust `str` or a pandas / polars string column; each is a module of its own with its own data (the per-code-point Bidi_Class and East_Asian_Width values are looked up, not applied) (`NFKC_Casefold` for IDNA / identifiers is already in `DerivedNormalizationProps.txt`).
- **A streaming normalizer object** (Go `norm.Reader` / `Writer`, Rust's iterator adaptors). *Not now:* the writer forms stream the output; the input must be one slice. A segment-at-a-time reader would let a caller normalize an unbounded file with constant memory.
- **`unaccent` where ICU's Latin-ASCII folds and this module does not** (`tools/latin_ascii_diff.py` names each case and fails when one appears unnamed). *Never*, by design: (a) compatibility forms — the 52 fullwidth Latin letters (Ａ → A), ŉ U+0149 (Latin-ASCII `'n`) and U+1DF95 LIGATURE LONG S WITH DESCENDER S (18.0, `<compat>` ß; a ligature `WITH` a second letter is not a letter with a mark): `unaccent` applies no compatibility mappings (use NFKC first); (b) non-letters — punctuation, symbols, fractions, Roman numerals, NO-BREAK SPACE, SOFT HYPHEN (« → `<<`, © → `(C)`, ½ → ` 1/2`): out of scope for an accent fold; (c) letters where Latin-ASCII is arbitrary: ɧ U+0267 HENG WITH HOOK (folded to h while HENG U+A727 itself is left alone; an IPA sound of its own), and the medieval abbreviation letters ꝱ ꝲ ꝳ ꝴ ꝵ ꝷ (DUM LUM MUM NUM RUM TUM) and ꝶ (SMALL CAPITAL RUM), which stand for a syllable: one letter loses it, and the syllable is a guess. The context rule of Latin-ASCII that writes `Ae` / `Oe` / `Th` for a capital ligature before a lowercase letter is not followed: `unaccent` maps per code point (`Œuvre` → `OEuvre`).
- **Locale option for `lower` / `upper` / `title`.** The first bullet above; CPython and Rust have none.
- **Dedupe with other modules.** `regex`'s General_Category / Script tables (`unicode_tables.zig`, built per `-Dregex-unicode` variant) and its simple case-fold orbits (`casefold.zig`), and `validate`'s `case_tables.zig`, are generated from the UCD by their own generators with their own goldens; deriving them from this module's tables would make `regex` and `validate` depend on `unitext` and move their goldens' anchor. No reference has such a thing: a cost with no consumer-visible gain, so each module keeps its generator.
- **A `size` knob that leaves out the compatibility decompositions** (about 40 % of the decomposition tables) for an NFC / NFD-only consumer. Go's `x/text` and Rust's `unicode-normalization` carry the compatibility tables unconditionally, and a build option here would split every test lane in two for 20 KB.
- **Stream-Safe Text Format enforcement** (UAX #15 Annex 15). *Not now:* `max_segment` bounds the cost instead.

## Open

- The fuzz harness has not been checked with planted mutants (a check that its reach classes really catch a broken algebra).
- The CPython column does not cover the 17,833 code points whose data changed between 16.0.0 and 18.0.0 (4,815 in 17.0, 13,016 in 18.0); Unicode's `NormalizationTest.txt` covers normalization for them and Rust covers lower / upper for the 17.0 ones, nothing foreign covers their classification (`isAlpha` …, new scripts) or title / casefold. Running the generator on UCD 16.0.0 and comparing *all* code points with CPython would close that (it needs a second build of the module with the 16.0.0 tables; not done: the intersection already compares 1.1 M code points).
